data.note:
Subjective
The Client reported a rough week, noting a panic attack on Tuesday at the grocery store checkout line with a pounding heart, which led them to leave their cart and walk out. The Client identified the automatic thought in the moment as believing they were going to pass out in front of everyone and that others would think they were crazy, rating this belief at 90 percent in the moment and 40 percent later at home. The Client completed two thought records out of the assigned three, covering the grocery store incident and an incident from work. Sleep was reported as poor, averaging about four hours a night with early morning awakening around 3:00 AM. The Client reported starting sertraline 50 mg approximately two weeks ago prescribed by their primary care doctor, noting initial nausea for the first few days which has since resolved. The Client denied any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation, stating they just want the panic to stop. The Client expressed frustration with their sister Dana's advice to "just push through it," feeling it is dismissive, and declined bringing the sister to a session at this time. Diagnosis: F41.0 Panic disorder.

Objective
Individual session, 50 minutes. Modality: CBT. The Therapist observed the Client to be cooperative and engaged throughout the session. During the in-session interoceptive exposure (spinning in the chair for 30 seconds), the Client rated their anxiety at a 6 out of 10 immediately following the exercise, which decreased to a 3 out of 10 within two minutes. Appearance, affect, and speech were otherwise not explicitly detailed in the transcript beyond active participation in clinical dialogue.

Assessment
The Client demonstrated progress toward treatment goals by utilizing the thought record to evaluate automatic thoughts, successfully reducing belief in the catastrophic thought from 90 percent to 40 percent retrospectively. The Client responded well to in-session interoceptive exposure, recognizing that physical sensations peak and pass without the need to escape, thereby reinforcing CBT principles for Panic Disorder (F41.0). Risk level for self-harm or suicide is assessed as none, as the Client explicitly denied any thoughts of hurting themselves or not wanting to be alive. The Client shows moderate engagement and a positive response to exposure-based interventions despite ongoing sleep disturbance and recent adjustment to pharmacotherapy.

Plan
Complete thought records three times this week. Practise the spinning interoceptive exposure exercise once a day at home. Attempt a return to the grocery store on a quiet Saturday morning and stay until anxiety drops by half. Attend next therapy session at the same time next week.
